def find_sidecar(script_path: Path) -> Path | None:

findings.why_relevant: Pre-execution gate: only checks sidecar presence/structural validity, first-of-kind, and adversarial_check DECLARED (not evaluated). Process/completion checks only, no scientific-validity check.

Post-execution: evaluates [outcomes.*].condition SQL fragments, first match wins. Mutually-exclusive branches, no 'all must hold, hard-fail on violation' semantics — the missing primitive for invariants.

Parsed and required-present in autonomous mode (prereg.py:287-301) but NEVER EVALUATED against the result at runtime (confirmed via grep — only tracked as a presence status string in runner.py:474-484/schema.py). Scaffold in new_experiment.py:61 shows original design intent as literal negation of the pass condition — closest existing half-built feature for req (1).

positive_outcome/negative_outcome label lists validated ONLY for existence in [outcomes] (validate.py:151); never evaluated/enforced — pure metadata consumed only by sprint_audit's control_arm_rate signal.

Near-miss for req (2): detects when all campaign runs share identical METADATA values (a 'single-cell gate smell'). But WARNING-only (bth lint, on-demand), checks run metadata not result/outcome values, and isn't a hard gate at run/conclude time — exactly the debt #200 complaint pattern (E==F==G) but downgraded to advisory.

Claim-tier (opt-in confirmatory/sequential campaigns only) cross-run hypothesis-discrimination: declares which planned run should separate which hypothesis pair; Union Gate downgrades verdict to 'confounded' if uncovered at conclude_campaign(). Real enforcement, but scoped to claim-tier only and about predicted-vs-actual outcome matching, not generic value-differs assertions.

EXACT semantic precedent for req (1): 'invariant_pass=False -> FAIL (hard floor)' cap-lattice grading, independent of other evidence dimensions. Scoped only to literature-parity attestation runs; invariant is a single self-reported boolean in the result dict (evidence_from_result), not an arbitrary sidecar-declared SQL predicate like [outcomes.*].condition.

Architectural precedent for a 'must satisfy X before this run counts' gate, but checks catalog HISTORY (a prior run passed), not a live synthetic-ground-truth check — req (3)'s [sanity] pre-flight block has zero prior art (confirmed via grep, no 'sanity' hits anywhere in src/bathos).

Structural-only validation (fields present, SQL parses, one residual branch) — confirms the debt's framing: bathos's structural/completion gates are unrelated to whether the SCIENTIFIC CONTENT of a result is trustworthy.
AC-13 reference_parity block (line 228+) is the closest precedent shape for both BP-2's synthetic_recovery confound and BP-3's structural validation
the actual enforcement-at-conclude pattern for confounds: computes per-confound controlled/uncontrolled status from live catalog state, fail-closed default uncontrolled

the real non-bypassable enforcement point bathos already uses: calls parity_confound_check + run_union_gate, downgrades outcome_label to 'confounded' for confirmation/sequential modes, warns for exploration. This is the native equivalent of asr's campaign-create hard block AND the closest thing bathos has to a per-conclusion verdict record (outcome_label + conclusion text).

confirmed campaign create takes only name/mode/question/hypothesis/parent -- no claim is attached yet at creation time, since claim register (claim.py:460) requires an already-existing campaign_id. This rules out a literal create-time hard block for synthetic_recovery (no claim exists yet to check).

Key files include postmortem.py (handling parsing and validation), sidecar.py (defining TOML blocks like ControlsBlock), and claim.py (referenced in validation logic). The 'Union Gate' was identified in the git history as a seam for campaigns, and the postmortem schema is defined in schema.py.
